session.question: How do PAs create public value in sustainability reporting?
session.answer:
Public administrations (PAs) create public value in sustainability reporting by using reporting as a governance mechanism that preserves and disseminates public value, strengthens legitimacy, and builds operational capacity. In the public value framework, sustainability reports make PA goals and actions visible, thereby helping align organizational activities with economic, social, and environmental objectives. (valenza2023sustainabilityreportingand chunk 1)

More specifically, the reporting process creates value through transparency, accountability, stakeholder participation, data gathering, measurement, and communication of progress. These practices support democratic accountability and improve the quality of governance around the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The Australian Senate inquiry evidence also indicates that public value is enhanced when business, investors, and civil society are involved and when there is strong central coordination. (abhayawansa2021accountabilityandgovernance chunk 1)

Sustainability reporting therefore functions not only as disclosure but as an institutional practice that can generate legitimacy and stakeholder support while improving decision-relevant information for national and supranational audiences. In this sense, PAs create public value by making sustainability performance observable, accountable, and usable for governance and decision-making. (valenza2023sustainabilityreportingand chunk 1, abhayawansa2021accountabilityandgovernance chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-68c8c4dc: The excerpt describes a study on how national governments can create value for society and the economy through their approach to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It argues that public administrations enhance public value by building accountability and governance systems centered on transparency, stakeholder participation, data gathering, measuring, and communicating progress. The Australian Senate inquiry evidence emphasized involving business, investors, civil society, and strong central coordination. The paper suggests that such sustainability reporting and governance mechanisms help governments improve social and economic value, and provide information useful for decision-making at both national and supranational levels.
From Subhash Abhayawansa, Carol A. Adams, and Cristina Neesham. Accountability and governance in pursuit of sustainable development goals: conceptualising how governments create value. Accounting Auditing & Accountability Journal, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.1108/aaaj-07-2020-4667, doi:10.1108/aaaj-07-2020-4667.

pqac-2aa0794d: The excerpt describes a 2021 paper arguing that national governments can create value for society and the economy through their approach to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It develops a conceptual framework from literature at the intersection of accountability, public policy, and sustainability. The study finds that submissions to an Australian Senate inquiry emphasized transparency, stakeholder participation, data gathering, measuring, and communicating, with involvement from business, investors, civil society, and strong central coordination. It frames sustainability-related accountability and governance as a way for governments/public administrations to enhance social and economic value, with implications for national governance and democratic accountability.
From Subhash Abhayawansa, Carol A. Adams, and Cristina Neesham. Accountability and governance in pursuit of sustainable development goals: conceptualising how governments create value. Accounting Auditing & Accountability Journal, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.1108/aaaj-07-2020-4667, doi:10.1108/aaaj-07-2020-4667.

pqac-b35cd598: The excerpt discusses integrated reporting (IR) as a sustainability-oriented reporting approach that aims to improve corporate reporting for stakeholders and increase transparency and accountability in capital markets. It proposes a theoretical framework combining stakeholder, agency, signalling, legitimacy, and institutional theories. According to the abstract, firms improve IR disclosure to mitigate information asymmetry with stakeholders, signal quality/legitimacy/conformity, and discharge accountability. These mechanisms suggest how public administrations can create public value in sustainability reporting: by enhancing transparency, accountability, legitimacy, and stakeholder-oriented disclosure. The paper also notes that high disclosure costs can hinder reporting quality and that the framework is intended as a foundation for future empirical work.
From Yanqi Sun, Howard Davey, Murugesh Arunachalam, and Yuanyuan Cao. Towards a theoretical framework for the innovation in sustainability reporting: an integrated reporting perspective. Frontiers in Environmental Science, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3389/fenvs.2022.935899, doi:10.3389/fenvs.2022.935899.

pqac-e5ce89c2: The excerpt says the paper studies how Italian Port Authorities create public value through sustainability reports, using the strategic triangle of public value. By analyzing the textual content of non-financial disclosures, the authors find that sustainability reporting helps PAs preserve and disseminate public value, obtain legitimacy and support from stakeholders, and build operational capacity. This suggests reporting is a mechanism for making actions visible to the public and stakeholders and for connecting sustainability goals with institutional legitimacy and organizational capacity. However, the excerpt does not give detailed discussion of specific mechanisms like transparency, accountability, comparability, trust, or decision usefulness.
From Giuseppe Valenza and Rodolfo Damiano. Sustainability reporting and public value: evidence from port authorities. Utilities Policy, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jup.2023.101508, doi:10.1016/j.jup.2023.101508.

pqac-b59647a4: The excerpt frames port authorities as public administrations that increasingly pursue economic, social, and environmental goals, and argues that scholars and policymakers should understand how they create public value. Using the strategic triangle framework of public value, the study analyzes non-financial disclosures in sustainability reports from eight Italian port authorities. It suggests that sustainability reporting is not just disclosure, but a practice through which public administrations preserve and disseminate public value, gain legitimacy and stakeholder support, and build operational capacity. The excerpt does not provide detailed evidence on performance, governance, environmental/social impact, or democratic accountability beyond this general public value perspective.
From Giuseppe Valenza and Rodolfo Damiano. Sustainability reporting and public value: evidence from port authorities. Utilities Policy, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jup.2023.101508, doi:10.1016/j.jup.2023.101508.

contexts.context: The excerpt discusses how sustainability reporting standards are shaped by international standard-setters (GSSB, ISSB, EFRAG) in response to environmental and social grand challenges. It emphasizes that standard-setting is not purely technical but a contested arena involving power struggles among stakeholders. Key issues include transparency, accountability, interoperability, materiality, and connectivity, with each board prioritizing different values (financial market relevance, stakeholder inclusivity, European public interest). The paper argues for more inclusive, transparent, and impactful approaches and notes that legitimacy and influence are continuously negotiated. However, it does not directly explain how public administrations create public value in sustainability reporting.

It argues that standard-setting bodies can use convening power, funding, membership choices, and agenda control to influence who participates and what issues are discussed. The paper says these collaborations generated input legitimacy for an investor-oriented vision of reporting focused on issues materially affecting enterprise value, while subtly sidelining the GRI approach. Although not about public administrations directly, the relevant mechanisms implied for public value in reporting are legitimacy, stakeholder inclusion, transparency of standard-setting, and comparability through standardisation.

session.formatted_answer:
Question: How do PAs create public value in sustainability reporting?

Public administrations (PAs) create public value in sustainability reporting by using reporting as a governance mechanism that preserves and disseminates public value, strengthens legitimacy, and builds operational capacity. In the public value framework, sustainability reports make PA goals and actions visible, thereby helping align organizational activities with economic, social, and environmental objectives. (valenza2023sustainabilityreportingand chunk 1)

More specifically, the reporting process creates value through transparency, accountability, stakeholder participation, data gathering, measurement, and communication of progress. These practices support democratic accountability and improve the quality of governance around the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The Australian Senate inquiry evidence also indicates that public value is enhanced when business, investors, and civil society are involved and when there is strong central coordination. (abhayawansa2021accountabilityandgovernance chunk 1)

Sustainability reporting therefore functions not only as disclosure but as an institutional practice that can generate legitimacy and stakeholder support while improving decision-relevant information for national and supranational audiences. In this sense, PAs create public value by making sustainability performance observable, accountable, and usable for governance and decision-making. (valenza2023sustainabilityreportingand chunk 1, abhayawansa2021accountabilityandgovernance chunk 1)
